questions.text: What is a Set in JavaScript?
distractors: A data structure that allows duplicate values.
A data structure that only stores strings and numbers.
A collection that does not allow deletion of its elements.
questions.answer: A collection in which a value can only occur once.

questions.text: Which of the following methods is available in Maps but not in Sets?

distractors: Managing key-value pairs in a database.
Storing hierarchical data structures in the browser local storage.

questions.text: What is a WeakSet in JavaScript?
distractors: A Set-like collection that only allows primitive data types.
A Set-like collection that allows duplicate values.
A Set-like collection that prevents values from being removed.
questions.answer: A Set-like collection that only stores objects.

questions.text: What is one difference between a Set and a WeakSet?
distractors: A WeakSet can store any type of value, including numbers.
A Set does not allow duplicate values, but a WeakSet does.
A Set allows garbage collection, whereas a WeakSet does not.
questions.answer: A Set can hold any type of value, while a WeakSet only holds objects.

questions.text: What is a Map in JavaScript?
distractors: A collection that only allows unique values.
A collection that can only use strings as keys.
A collection that does not allow deletion of its items.
questions.answer: A collection of key-value pairs of any type.

questions.text: What method is used to insert key-value pairs into a Map?
How does a Map differ from an Object in JavaScript?
distractors: A Map only allows numbers as keys.
Objects allow any type as keys, while Maps only allow strings.
Maps do not support iteration, while Objects do.
questions.answer: Maps allow any type of key, but Objects only allow strings and symbols.

questions.text: How can you remove a key-value pair from a Map?
What does the `size` property of a Map return?
distractors: The number of indexes in the Map.
The number of unique values in the Map.
The total memory used by the Map.
questions.answer: The number of key-value pairs in the Map.

questions.text: What is a WeakMap in JavaScript?
distractors: A Map-like collection that allows primitive values as keys.
A Map-like collection that blocks the deletion of items.
A Map-like collection that automatically sorts its keys.
questions.answer: A Map-like collection with weak references to the keys.

questions.text: What is one difference between a Map and a WeakMap?
distractors: A Map allows only primitive types as keys, whereas a WeakMap only allows objects.
A Map allows garbage collection, whereas a WeakMap does not.
A WeakMap allows duplicate keys, whereas a Map does not.
questions.answer: A Map is iterable, whereas a WeakMap is not.
